chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn Ahmad, from Ahmad ibn al-Husayn, from Amr ibn Saeed, from Musaddiq ibn Sadaqa, from Ammar al-Sabati, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), from his father (peace be upon him), regarding

a man who made it upon himself to free a slave, and he freed a lame [or] a paralytic. He (peace be upon him) said: 'If he was from what is being sold, it would suffice for him, except if he had specified [a particular slave], so upon him would be what he had stipulated and specified.'
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling if a man vows to free a slave but frees a defective one?
ai.summary: This hadith clarifies the conditions for fulfilling a vow of manumission (kaffarat al-yamin) by distinguishing between general and specific vows; if the vow was general, freeing any commonly traded slave with a defect suffices, but if a specific individual was named, that exact person must be freed. This ruling reflects the Shia juristic principle that the specificity of the vow dictates the precision of the fulfillment, ensuring the vow's intent is met without undue hardship unless explicitly required. It highlights the importance of intent (niyyah) and linguistic precision in Islamic legal obligations.

en.hubeali:
Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Muhammad Bin Ahmad, from Ahmad Bin Al Husayn, from Amro Bin Saeed, from Musadda Bin Sadaqa, from Ammar Al Sabity, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> from his<sup>asws</sup> father<sup>asws</sup> regarding

a man who made it upon himself to the freeing of a neck, be he paralysed or lame. He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘If he was from what is being sold, it would suffice from it, except he happened to have specified it, so upon him would be what he had stipulated and specified’.
en.sarwar: 16. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Ahmad ibn al-Husayn from ‘Amr ibn Sa‘id from Musaddiq ibn Sadaqah from ‘Ammar al-Sabatiy who has narrated the following: “About the case of a man who makes it upon himself to free a slave then sets free a paralyzed or lame one, abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, Tf he is sellable, it is sufficient unless he has specified, in which case he must meet the condition.’”
